svg.text: A window 1250 px wide at a screen scale of 2.3 (about 540 units: a rack's width), as on your screenshots.
The numbers are listed under the pictures.
DECIDED · top panel: B, folding into MORE (logo first, then grey keys, then groups from the right); ALIGN is off in RACK
DECIDED · ENGINE's strip: A, what matters first, the rest behind i; SAVE REPORT lives on DIAGNOSTICS' tab row; its key aligned
DECIDED · the line about the open table: in the status bar while over the tabs · the status bar: the hints go first, then the left text ends in …
ENGINE, a node chosen, the tables open
1 The top panel is one row: past LAYOUT its keys are cut off. LOCK, ALIGN, CABLES, VIEW, CUE · LEVEL and the LCD (defaults, preset) can't be reached.
2 ENGINE's strip drops the cells that don't fit, from the end: CLOCK, QUANTUM, DRIVERS, DSP LOAD, XRUNS go; SERVER and SESSION, the least needed, stay.
3 ALSO SHOW's chips run on under the details: NOT RUNNING cut, INTERNAL gone.
4 The details' tabs and rows are cut at the right: TIMING, and long values wrap into many lines.
5 The tables' tabs and the line about the open table are drawn over each other.
6 The status bar's two texts are drawn over each other.
7 The tables' columns run off the right edge (W/Q, B/Q, ERR, FORMAT, NAME); the graph is left a sliver, drawn tiny.
THE TOP PANEL · B: WHAT DOESN'T FIT FOLDS INTO MORE
When the panel is too wide for the window, in this order: 1. the logo goes, all of it; 2. grey keys go (what this screen can't use:
LOCK and ALIGN in ENGINE, ALIGN in RACK, where it is off now; in ENGINE CABLES, CUE · LEVEL and VIEW but FIT too); 3. groups fold into MORE ▾ from the right:
LCD, CUE · LEVEL, VIEW, CABLES, LOCK · ALIGN, EDIT. DESK · RACK · ENGINE never fold. MORE drops the folded groups below the panel, as they look.
in MORE: LCD · CUE · LEVEL · VIEW
in MORE: LCD · CUE · LEVEL · VIEW · CABLES · ALIGN · LOCK
in MORE: LCD · CUE · LEVEL · VIEW
in MORE: LCD · CUE · LEVEL · VIEW · CABLES · LOCK
MORE, OPEN · DESK AT 540 UNITS: THE FOLDED GROUPS DROP BELOW THE PANEL, IN THEIR ORDER, AS MANY ROWS AS THEY NEED
the LCD's two halves, each in its own row
when a row can't hold it whole
ENGINE'S STRIP · A: WHAT MATTERS FIRST
CLOCK, QUANTUM, DSP LOAD, XRUNS, HEALTH; SERVER, SESSION, ALLOWED, DRIVERS and OBJECTS behind the i cell (its card drops under it).
SAVE REPORT is gone from here, for good: it is a key on DIAGNOSTICS' tab row.
900 UNITS: ALL BUT THE i CELL'S FIT; DSP LOAD'S CURVE TOO
DIAGNOSTICS · ITS KEY, ALIGNED; SAVE REPORT ON ITS TAB ROW
the chevron sits low and its text high: both on the key's middle, the same gap to the edges
the tab row at 540 units: the tabs, SAVE REPORT, the fold key
Two lines ran over things: the line about the open table, and the status bar's two texts. At 540 units.
THE LINE ABOUT THE OPEN TABLE
CHOSEN · IN THE STATUS BAR, WHILE THE POINTER IS OVER THE TABS (AS FOR ANY KEY); THE TAB ROW HOLDS ONLY ITS TABS AND KEYS
TOP: as pw-top: each driver and the nodes it clocks; the last half…
CHOSEN · THE HINTS ON THE RIGHT GO FIRST, THEN THE LEFT TEXT ENDS IN …
ENGINE · what PipeWire really has · 15 nodes · 37 ports…
These are faults whichever way the panel goes.
3 ALSO SHOW's chips wrap onto a second row inside the graph's part.
4 The details panel never takes more than half the window; in a window under 700 units it opens over the graph (graph full width under it).
7 The tables keep the columns that say most (S, ID, BUSY, ERR, NAME) and drop the others from the right when narrow; the rest scroll sideways.
